By means of this C482 application, the applicant had challenged the summoning and cognizance order dated 13.10.2017, passed by learned Judicial Magistrate Bajpur, District Udham Singh Nagar as well as the charge-sheet and the entire proceedings of Criminal Case No. 812 of 2017, State Vs.
Mohan Singh, under Sections 420 of IPC and Section 12 of The Passport Act, 1967 (for short "the Act").
2.

entities.text: Judicial Magistrate Bajpur, District Udham Singh Nagar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The challenge launched by the applicant is on a very limited ground.

3. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that after submission of the charge-sheet, the trial court vide order dated 13.10.2017 took cognizance of the matter and issued summons against the applicant - accused to appear before the court to face the trial under Section 420 of IPC and Section 12 of the Act.

It is further submitted that this is a cyclostyle order and apparently, learned Judicial Magistrate has not applied his mind to the material submitted during investigation in the police report.
4.
The F.I.R. has been lodged by Sub-Inspector, L.I.U - Manoj Kumar on 02.01.2017 at 20:12 hours in Police Station Bazpur, District Udham Singh Nagar against the applicant - Mohan Singh.
On the basis of which F.I.R. No. 0005 of 2017 was registered under Section 420 and Section 12 of the Act.
5. In brief, case of the prosecution, as unfolded, from the F.I.R is that the informant conducted an inquiry regarding the passport of the applicant - Mohan Singh S/o Seva Singh.

During inquiry, in Mohan Singh vs State Of Uttarakhand & Another on 20 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189836541/
1 respect of the passport application moved by Mohan Singh, it was found that there was a criminal case registered against the applicant, which has been disclosed in the F.I.R., but the applicant in order to obtain the passport suppressed this material fact, in his application, which was a violation of the provisions of Section 12 of the Act.

6. I have perused the charge-sheet as well as the documents filed in support of the C482 application,
it was found that the learned Judicial Magistrate took cognizance of the matter and recorded it, on the charge- sheet, and signed it on 13.10.2017 and accordingly, the same was transcribed and signed by the learned Judicial Magistrate, on the order sheet, on the same date.

7. Learned counsel for the applicant has placed reliance upon a judgment rendered by a Co-ordinate Bench of this Court, dated 10.11.2022 in C482 application No. 2004 of 2022, Tarun @ Swami Tribhuwan Das Vs. State of Uttarakhand and others, whereby a Co- ordinate Bench after hearing learned counsel for the applicant quashed the summoning order dated 16.12.2017 and remitted the matter back to the learned Judicial Magistrate to pass a fresh order,
after assigning and justifying the reasons for summoning the accused in that case.

sentences.text: I have gone through the case laws and am of view that these precedents shall not apply to the facts of the case in hand for the reasons that in the present case the learned Judicial Magistrate passed the order taking cognizance on the charge-sheet on 13.10.2017.

The case in hand, the charge-sheet was submitted by police along with a record and the learned Judicial Magistrate had applied its mind and passed an order dated 13.10.2017, which is reflected from the charge-sheet itself and thereafter, the same order was transcribed in order sheet dated 13.10.2017.
It has been settled by the Hon'ble Apex Court that while summoning the accused, no detail reasons are required by the Judicial Magistrate.

Herein, the case at hand, learned Judicial Magistrate has passed an order while taking cognizance, which is quoted hereunder:-
"vfHk;qDr eksgu flag ds fo: /kkjk 420 IPC o 12 ikliksVZ Act1967 ds vijk/k dk laKku fy;k x;kA ntZ jft0 gksA Sd. J.M. 13.10.2017"
10.

From this order of taking cognizance, it is amply clear that the learned Judicial Magistrate has applied his mind and took cognizance, and, thereafter, the summoning order dated 13.10.2017,
passed by learned Judicial Magistrate.
The applicant failed to show that it's a case where there is no application of mind of learned Judicial Magistrate.
